title: Covariate Model Selection Approaches for Population Pharmacokinetics: A Systematic Review of Existing Methods, From SCM to AI

content.abstract_summary: Systematic review of all covariate modeling methods in population pharmacokinetics, from traditional stepwise covariate modeling (SCM) through modern AI/ML alternatives. Reviews evaluation settings, performance metrics, and computational times for each method across the literature. Main conclusion: EBE-based ML methods stood out as the best covariate selection methods for prescreening; AALASSO (a hybrid genetic algorithm) was the overall best covariate model selection technique. Proposes standardized benchmarking and reporting practices for future method comparisons. From Montpellier University + Sanofi R&D, published in CPT:PSP.
key_findings: EBE-based ML methods (using Empirical Bayes Estimates as targets for ML covariate selection) are the best covariate prescreening approach across the methods reviewed — faster and more accurate than traditional graphical correlations or GAM

AALASSO (Adaptive LASSO hybrid with genetic algorithm) is the best overall covariate model selection technique — outperforms standard SCM, SCM+, SAMBA, LASSO, Wald's approximation, and FREM in systematic comparison
FREM (full random effects model with clinical significance criterion) and SCM+ with stagewise filtering are the next best approaches after AALASSO
No consensus on how to benchmark simulated datasets across scenarios or which performance metrics to use — the field lacks standardized evaluation, making method comparisons unreliable

Proposed standardized metrics: TPR (sensitivity), FPR (Type I error), FNR (Type II error), TNR (specificity), covariate parameter error bias (MPE), and precision (RMSE), plus model fitness by BIC and concentration prediction error
Recommendation: new methods should always be compared against SCM as a baseline; covariate selection techniques should be combined with SCM or FFEM for head-to-head comparison
limitations: Review is limited to published comparisons of method performance — unpublished industry practice (likely dominated by SCM) is not captured
Lack of standardized benchmarking datasets makes quantitative cross-study comparison difficult; the review identifies this as the main obstacle to progress in the field
Most comparisons lack external validation — performance rankings may be simulation-scenario-specific

extracted_claims.text: EBEs-based ML methods stood out as the best covariate selection methods. AALASSO, a hybrid genetic algorithm, FREM with a clinical significance criterion and SCM+ with stagewise filtering were the best covariate model selection techniques — AALASSO being the very best one.
We also highlight the need for an open-source benchmark of simulated datasets on a representative set of scenarios.

gaps_addressed: Provides the definitive landscape map for M1.3 (ML for covariate selection in pop PK) — any WG tutorial or scoping paper covering ML in pharmacometrics should cite this systematic review as the reference for covariate selection methods
The AALASSO finding (best overall method) vs EBE-ML (best prescreening) is a concrete recommendation the WG can build on for hybrid pharmacometric workflows
The call for open-source benchmarks maps directly to the WG's potential contribution: creating benchmark datasets for hybrid methods is a concrete, achievable WG deliverable
